_note: Hackathon draft, not legal advice. The rules engine evaluates 'condition' against the user profile and shows matching cards. The model only explains the card in plain English using the linked topic file. Fields used: income_self, income_spouse, has_children, years_married, has_access_to_accounts, owns_home, case_filed, stage.

rules.because: Because you earn less than your spouse
rules.title: You may be able to ask for help with bills while your case is open
rules.summary: The court can order your spouse to help with living costs during the case, based on your need and their ability to pay.

rules.because: Because you earn less than your spouse
rules.title: You may be able to ask your spouse to help pay for your lawyer
rules.summary: If there is a gap in access to legal help and your spouse can pay for both sides, the court can order them to contribute.

rules.because: Because every divorcing spouse must disclose
rules.title: Your spouse has to show you their finances too
rules.summary: Both sides must share income, assets and debts, at filing or within 60 days.

rules.because: Because you don't have full access to the family accounts
rules.title: We can help you find what to ask about
rules.summary: Upload what you can find. We'll flag possible gaps, like income with no matching account, to add to your lawyer brief.

rules.because: Because your case hasn't been filed yet
rules.title: Forms to start your case
rules.summary: The petition and summons start the case and tell your spouse.

rules.because: Because you have children with your spouse
rules.title: An extra form about your children
rules.summary: Add FL-105 at filing, which covers where your children have lived.

rules.because: Because court fees may be hard to afford on your income
rules.title: You may be able to skip court filing fees
rules.summary: A fee waiver lets you file without paying the fee if you qualify.

rules.title: The earliest your divorce can be final is six months and a day
rules.summary: The clock starts when your spouse is served and cannot be shortened. Contested cases usually take longer.
